result.description: Hermes Agent, examined at repository commit 97246dfcc2d9853fc5b5aad3829dba8d7d7335d4. The artifact implements an autonomous agent that conducts conversations, calls tools, performs digital tasks, retains knowledge and procedures, delegates work, and runs automations through several client interfaces. This map groups implementations by their functional contribution. All 20,933 tracked paths were inventoried; Python modules were structurally surveyed, and implementation bodies were traced across the principal functional systems. External integrations were not exercised. CQU identities are functional inferences. No confirmed broken or missing functionality is asserted from source inspection alone. ICE blocks are not assigned where indivisible coupling was not established.

join.purpose: Complete digital work through a persistent assistant that can act on requests and reuse accumulated knowledge.
join.function: Interprets requests, alternates model inference with tool execution, and returns task results across conversations.
join.ef: Interprets requests, alternates model inference with tool execution, and returns task results across conversations.
join.observation: Inferred principal CQU: the party whose recurring research, writing, analysis, and computing tasks drive improvements in task completion, continuity, and learned procedures.

join.purpose: Carry out recurring and coordinated work with retained execution state and delivery of its results.
join.function: Executes scheduled, event-triggered, goal-directed, and delegated work through the shared agent runtime.
join.ef: Executes scheduled, event-triggered, goal-directed, and delegated work through the shared agent runtime.
join.observation: Inferred CQU distinguished by responsibility for the continuing outcome of an automation, rather than responsibility for operating the software.

join.purpose: Produce and examine tool-using agent trajectories for evaluation and model training.
join.function: Runs agent tasks over datasets and exposes recorded conversations, tool interactions, and compressed trajectories.
join.ef: Runs agent tasks over datasets and exposes recorded conversations, tool interactions, and compressed trajectories.
join.observation: Inferred secondary CQU supported by explicit batch execution, trajectory export, compression, and evaluation functionality.

join.purpose: Obtain model decisions, responses, and tool calls throughout task execution.
join.function: Routes inference requests and normalizes provider responses for the common agent loop.
join.ef: Routes inference requests and normalizes provider responses for the common agent loop.
join.observation: The agent loop retains tool execution and turn termination while provider-specific transports translate requests, streams, usage, reasoning, and tool calls.

join.purpose: Receive generated responses from a compatible model service.
join.function: Accepts model requests and returns generated text, structured tool calls, reasoning, or streaming events.
join.ef: Accepts model requests and returns generated text, structured tool calls, reasoning, or streaming events.
join.observation: Implemented routes include OpenAI-compatible chat completions, Responses, Anthropic Messages, Bedrock, Gemini, Codex app-server, and ACP-backed inference bridges; support depends on the selected route.

join.purpose: Authenticate model requests and recover supported credential failures.
join.function: Resolves credential sources, refreshes supported tokens, and rotates eligible pooled credentials.
join.ef: Resolves credential sources, refreshes supported tokens, and rotates eligible pooled credentials.
join.observation: Credential identity, provider routing, cooldowns, and persistence are handled separately from response-format conversion.

join.purpose: Acquire credentials accepted by the selected external service.
join.function: Issues or supplies API credentials, OAuth grants, or credentials resolved through configured secret sources.
join.ef: Issues or supplies API credentials, OAuth grants, or credentials resolved through configured secret sources.
join.observation: Credentials can originate in configuration, environment files, supported account stores, commands, or external secret-source integrations.

join.purpose: Use supported locally hosted models through a managed inference endpoint.
join.function: Acquires compatible runtime binaries, supervises llama-server, and resolves local model endpoints.
join.ef: Acquires compatible runtime binaries, supervises llama-server, and resolves local model endpoints.
join.observation: The managed local runtime includes hardware inspection, model browsing, model metadata, context-memory estimation, loading progress, and runtime recovery.

join.purpose: Present the model with instructions and working history that remain usable across continued execution.
join.function: Assembles session instructions, selects working context, and coordinates context reduction.
join.ef: Assembles session instructions, selects working context, and coordinates context reduction.
join.observation: System-prompt snapshots and historical message prefixes are preserved across ordinary turns; turn-local additions use current-turn content rather than routine prompt reconstruction.

join.purpose: Ground each session in its instructions, available capabilities, and relevant environment.
join.function: Builds the system prompt from identity, context files, memory snapshots, skill information, and platform or plugin sections.
join.ef: Builds the system prompt from identity, context files, memory snapshots, skill information, and platform or plugin sections.
join.observation: Instruction-file discovery, context references, skill preprocessing, platform hints, and frozen plugin sections contribute to the assembled prompt.

join.purpose: Continue conversations when accumulated context approaches the selected model's capacity.
join.function: Prunes eligible results, preserves protected history, and summarizes or delegates supported native compaction.
join.ef: Prunes eligible results, preserves protected history, and summarizes or delegates supported native compaction.
join.observation: The default engine combines deterministic reduction with auxiliary-model summarization. Compaction coordinates stored history, active rows, provider-specific carriers, and client-visible summaries.

join.purpose: Reuse durable knowledge and procedures across otherwise separate conversations.
join.function: Combines curated memory, procedural skills, historical recall, and maintenance of learned material.
join.ef: Combines curated memory, procedural skills, historical recall, and maintenance of learned material.
join.observation: The built-in memory provider can operate with one selected external provider. The implemented learning loop stores and retrieves information; improvement depends on what the model elects to retain and apply.

join.purpose: Retain selected facts and personal context beyond the current session.
join.function: Reads and modifies profile-local memory entries and supplies a frozen session-start snapshot.
join.ef: Reads and modifies profile-local memory entries and supplies a frozen session-start snapshot.
join.observation: MEMORY.md and USER.md hold distinct memory targets. Mid-session writes persist to disk without replacing the current session's frozen prompt snapshot.

join.purpose: Retain reusable instructions and load their detail when a task needs them.
join.function: Discovers, lists, reads, creates, patches, and manages skill packages and their supporting files.
join.ef: Discovers, lists, reads, creates, patches, and manages skill packages and their supporting files.
join.observation: Skill metadata supports progressive disclosure; full instructions and linked resources are loaded separately. Bundled and optional skill collections retain member identity through their paths.

join.purpose: Recover relevant information from earlier conversations.
join.function: Searches stored sessions and returns matching conversation material with optional model-assisted synthesis.
join.ef: Searches stored sessions and returns matching conversation material with optional model-assisted synthesis.
join.observation: Historical recall is distinct from curated memory: it searches retained conversation records rather than requiring facts to have been copied into the memory files.

join.purpose: Access retained conversations as searchable records.
join.function: Provides stored session messages and full-text search indexes.
join.ef: Provides stored session messages and full-text search indexes.

join.purpose: Turn useful execution experience into maintained memory and skills.
join.function: Reviews conversation snapshots and performs configured background or idle maintenance of retained material.
join.ef: Reviews conversation snapshots and performs configured background or idle maintenance of retained material.
join.observation: Background review forks inspect completed work without modifying the foreground transcript. Idle curation separately manages skill lifecycle, consolidation, archiving, and recoverable backups.

join.purpose: Continue the correct conversation and preserve ownership of its queued and running work.
join.function: Routes session inputs, serializes admissions, manages execution ownership, and publishes committed results.
join.ef: Routes session inputs, serializes admissions, manages execution ownership, and publishes committed results.
join.observation: The shared gateway owns canonical local-session execution. Viewers submit inputs and observe results; reconnecting a viewer does not independently recreate the execution owner.

join.purpose: Persist conversation identity, history, execution state, and results for continued use and recovery.
join.function: Maintains canonical session records, messages, lineage, metadata, usage, and transactional execution receipts.
join.ef: Maintains canonical session records, messages, lineage, metadata, usage, and transactional execution receipts.
join.observation: SessionDB uses SQLite with WAL, multiple readers, and a writer boundary. Its supporting modules implement mutations, compression history, rewind, branching, media, search, maintenance, and recovery.

join.purpose: Retain committed state and related files across process lifetimes.
join.function: Provides writable persistent files and the filesystem operations required by the database and stores.
join.ef: Provides writable persistent files and the filesystem operations required by the database and stores.
join.observation: Conversation databases, configuration, memory, skills, cron state, caches, and execution receipts use profile-aware storage locations.

join.purpose: Turn model-selected operations into observable actions and results.
join.function: Resolves tool calls, applies the dispatch pipeline, invokes handlers, and returns normalized results.
join.ef: Resolves tool calls, applies the dispatch pipeline, invokes handlers, and returns normalized results.
join.observation: The agent persists tool-call messages before side effects and persists tool results before subsequent inference. Dispatch carries task, session, turn, and request identity through hooks and middleware.

join.purpose: Associate available tool schemas with their executable handlers.
join.function: Discovers tool registrations and resolves schema, availability, ownership, scope, and dispatch metadata.
join.ef: Discovers tool registrations and resolves schema, availability, ownership, scope, and dispatch metadata.
join.observation: Built-in discovery and plugin registrations converge on the registry; toolsets select combinations without requiring a separate execution implementation.

join.purpose: Expose a large capability set without placing every tool definition in every model request.
join.function: Lists and describes deferred tools and unwraps selected calls into the ordinary dispatch pipeline.
join.ef: Lists and describes deferred tools and unwraps selected calls into the ordinary dispatch pipeline.
join.observation: tool_search, tool_describe, and tool_call provide progressive tool disclosure using the live definitions available to the session.

join.purpose: Run shell commands in the workspace selected for a task.
join.function: Executes commands through a common environment interface with working-directory, interruption, and output handling.
join.ef: Executes commands through a common environment interface with working-directory, interruption, and output handling.
join.observation: Built-in backends include local execution, Docker, SSH, Modal, Daytona, and Vercel Sandbox. Persistent cloud filesystems do not imply preservation of live processes.

join.purpose: Obtain a host capable of running the selected shell and task processes.
join.function: Provides operating-system process execution, working files, and backend-specific execution facilities.
join.ef: Provides operating-system process execution, working files, and backend-specific execution facilities.
join.observation: Execution can depend on a local host, container engine, SSH destination, or configured remote sandbox service.

join.purpose: Continue and inspect commands that outlive a foreground tool call.
join.function: Tracks background processes, captures output, accepts control operations, and reports completion.
join.ef: Tracks background processes, captures output, accepts control operations, and reports completion.
join.observation: Process handling includes checkpointed identity, termination, bounded result receipts, and completion notifications to the originating execution context.

join.purpose: Inspect and modify task files through explicit file operations.
join.function: Reads, searches, writes, and patches files across supported execution backends.
join.ef: Reads, searches, writes, and patches files across supported execution backends.
join.observation: The implementation includes path resolution, fuzzy replacement, read tracking, concurrent file coordination, syntax checks, and optional language-server diagnostic deltas.

join.purpose: Perform multi-step computation and tool coordination within a single model-directed operation.
join.function: Runs generated Python in a session kernel and exposes selected Hermes tools through RPC.
join.ef: Runs generated Python in a session kernel and exposes selected Hermes tools through RPC.
join.observation: Local and remote kernels support reusable execution state; script stdout returns to the model and oversized output can be spilled. README's zero-context-cost wording overstates the mechanism: script calls and returned output still enter the conversation.

join.purpose: Inspect and operate websites that require interactive browsing.
join.function: Runs browser automation against a managed local, remote, cloud, or connected browser session.
join.ef: Runs browser automation against a managed local, remote, cloud, or connected browser session.
join.observation: Browser execution includes session lifecycle, CDP access, dialog handling, frame tracking, profile handling, and backend placement.

join.purpose: Fill supported website credentials without exposing their secret values to the model.
join.function: Resolves saved logins and performs controlled credential autofill through the browser integration.
join.ef: Resolves saved logins and performs controlled credential autofill through the browser integration.
join.observation: The vault supports a local encrypted backend and external password-manager backends, with unlock and account-selection interactions.

join.purpose: Perform tasks through application windows and desktop input.
join.function: Captures desktop state and sends pointer, keyboard, and other supported control actions.
join.ef: Captures desktop state and sends pointer, keyboard, and other supported control actions.
join.observation: Computer use is implemented through provider backends. Bot Desktop additionally provides a profile-owned headless desktop with remote viewing and control ownership.

join.purpose: Find external sources relevant to a task.
join.function: Queries a selected search provider and returns source metadata and result locations.
join.ef: Queries a selected search provider and returns source metadata and result locations.
join.observation: Search providers are pluggable. Web search and X search have separate implementations; result caching and provider selection support repeated retrieval.

join.purpose: Receive results and content from reachable external web services.
join.function: Supplies search responses, retrieved pages, and service-specific network responses.
join.ef: Supplies search responses, retrieved pages, and service-specific network responses.
join.observation: Required destinations depend on configured search, extraction, browsing, and tool-service providers.

join.purpose: Read the substance of located external documents.
join.function: Retrieves page content and returns extracted text with recoverable handling of oversized results.
join.ef: Retrieves page content and returns extracted text with recoverable handling of oversized results.
join.observation: web_extract performs content extraction rather than automatic LLM summarization; large results use an inline window and stored full-text reference.

join.purpose: Interpret visual material supplied by a task or encountered during execution.
join.function: Prepares images or video material and obtains model-assisted visual analysis.
join.ef: Prepares images or video material and obtains model-assisted visual analysis.
join.observation: vision_analyze and video_analyze handle distinct inputs while sharing model routing, source resolution, and visual-content preparation.

join.purpose: Create or transform visual deliverables requested by a task.
join.function: Dispatches supported image and video generation or editing requests and returns generated output references.
join.ef: Dispatches supported image and video generation or editing requests and returns generated output references.
join.observation: Image and video generation use separate provider contracts and catalogs; available editing operations depend on the chosen provider and model.

join.purpose: Invoke capabilities supplied by independently hosted tool servers.
join.function: Connects to MCP servers, discovers supported capabilities, and translates their calls and results into Hermes dispatch.
join.ef: Connects to MCP servers, discovers supported capabilities, and translates their calls and results into Hermes dispatch.
join.observation: Implemented transports include stdio, Streamable HTTP, and SSE. Supporting functions handle schemas, resources, prompts, OAuth, reconnects, server lifecycle, and optional experimental events.

join.purpose: Obtain capabilities conforming to the configured MCP connection.
join.function: Advertises and serves its available tools, resources, prompts, or supported extensions.
join.ef: Advertises and serves its available tools, resources, prompts, or supported extensions.
join.observation: A server must be reachable and satisfy the configured transport and authentication requirements; advertised capabilities determine what Hermes exposes.

join.purpose: Apply the configured authority and execution policies to requested actions.
join.function: Evaluates operation policies, obtains supported human decisions, and enforces resulting dispatch decisions.
join.ef: Evaluates operation policies, obtains supported human decisions, and enforces resulting dispatch decisions.
join.observation: Existing mechanisms cover command approval, file and instruction protections, memory and skill write policies, website policy, and computer-use approval. These are observed project behavior.

join.purpose: Recover workspace state after supported file-mutating operations.
join.function: Creates workspace snapshots and restores selected checkpoints through a shadow Git store.
join.ef: Creates workspace snapshots and restores selected checkpoints through a shadow Git store.
join.observation: Checkpointing is host infrastructure rather than a model-visible tool; retention and pruning manage its stored history.

join.purpose: Divide work among agents and combine their contributions.
join.function: Constructs child agents, routes their tasks, exposes progress and controls, and returns or asynchronously delivers results.
join.ef: Constructs child agents, routes their tasks, exposes progress and controls, and returns or asynchronously delivers results.
join.observation: Delegation supports synchronous and background execution, per-task routing, grouped completion, independent child histories, result processing, and originating-session delivery.

join.purpose: Coordinate durable dependent tasks and assign eligible work to execution workers.
join.function: Maintains task boards and dependency state, dispatches workers, and records task lifecycle events.
join.ef: Maintains task boards and dependency state, dispatches workers, and records task lifecycle events.
join.observation: Kanban includes atomic decomposition, task readiness, cross-profile assignment, worker liveness, failure accounting, review dispatch, notifications, and workspace selection.

join.purpose: Maintain the agent's current multi-step work list.
join.function: Stores and revises task-list entries and projects them into supported client plan displays.
join.ef: Stores and revises task-list entries and projects them into supported client plan displays.
join.observation: todo_list is distinct from the durable Kanban dispatch board; task-list state is revisioned and can be hydrated from conversation history.

join.purpose: Use multiple model contributions within a selected agent turn.
join.function: Collects reference-model guidance for an aggregator while retaining the ordinary agent tool loop.
join.ef: Collects reference-model guidance for an aggregator while retaining the ordinary agent tool loop.
join.observation: Mixture-of-Agents is a selected turn mode rather than the replacement owner of tool execution or turn termination.

join.purpose: Exchange work and discussion between independently situated agents or profiles.
join.function: Routes bot messages and hosted group interactions with retained membership, task, attachment, and execution identities.
join.ef: Routes bot messages and hosted group interactions with retained membership, task, attachment, and execution identities.
join.observation: Bot Chat, cross-connection relay, and gateway-owned Group Chats provide collaboration distinct from constructing local delegate_task children.

join.purpose: Perform work at scheduled times or continue an active objective without a fresh manual request.
join.function: Schedules durable jobs and supplies session-scoped goal, loop, and heartbeat continuations.
join.ef: Schedules durable jobs and supplies session-scoped goal, loop, and heartbeat continuations.
join.observation: Durable cron scheduling and live-session continuations have different lifetimes; stored continuation state does not itself provide an independent scheduler process.

join.purpose: Persist recurring or one-time jobs and execute their scheduled occurrences.
join.function: Claims due jobs, runs agent-backed or script jobs, records outcomes, and delivers configured results.
join.ef: Claims due jobs, runs agent-backed or script jobs, records outcomes, and delivers configured results.
join.observation: Cron includes occurrence identity, execution bookkeeping, monitor change suppression, per-job state, failure incidents, worker recovery, and delivery. Blueprints package reusable skill-and-schedule automations.

join.purpose: Continue a session toward an active objective or recurring session instruction.
join.function: Evaluates goal completion and inserts ordinary continuation or timed wakeup prompts into eligible sessions.
join.ef: Evaluates goal completion and inserts ordinary continuation or timed wakeup prompts into eligible sessions.
join.observation: Goals use auxiliary-model judgments; loops and heartbeats provide recurring re-entry. Heartbeats yield to real queued input, and the live CLI or gateway drives session wakeups.

join.purpose: Receive task requests, present execution, and accept interaction through supported clients.
join.function: Projects conversations and controls into command-line, terminal, desktop, browser, voice, and programming interfaces.
join.ef: Projects conversations and controls into command-line, terminal, desktop, browser, voice, and programming interfaces.
join.observation: Client interfaces share agent and session functions while providing different input, rendering, attachment, interaction, and control mechanisms.

join.purpose: Conduct interactive conversations and administer Hermes from a shell.
join.function: Provides a REPL, slash commands, session controls, and command-line administration.
join.ef: Provides a REPL, slash commands, session controls, and command-line administration.
join.observation: The CLI facade and mixins implement input, streaming presentation, interruption, commands, and integration with shared session functionality.

join.purpose: Use a structured conversational interface within a terminal.
join.function: Renders interactive conversation state and sends canonical session operations through the terminal client.
join.ef: Renders interactive conversation state and sends canonical session operations through the terminal client.
join.observation: The Ink TUI includes editing, command discovery, history, tool presentation, and request/result projection for the shared gateway.

join.purpose: Manage conversations, workspaces, deliverables, and connected capabilities in a desktop application.
join.function: Combines chat with terminals, previews, artifacts, agent views, connection management, and desktop integration.
join.ef: Combines chat with terminals, previews, artifacts, agent views, connection management, and desktop integration.
join.observation: The Electron application includes local and remote backend connections, profiles, automation controls, capability discovery, overlays, notifications, and contributed interface surfaces.

join.purpose: Inspect and configure a Hermes installation through a browser.
join.function: Serves administration pages, backend APIs, and an embedded terminal chat interface.
join.ef: Serves administration pages, backend APIs, and an embedded terminal chat interface.
join.observation: Dashboard pages cover sessions, files, logs, models, configuration, profiles, skills, plugins, channels, pairing, MCP, webhooks, analytics, and cron.

join.purpose: Accept agent requests from external programs.
join.function: Exposes agent execution through HTTP APIs, compatible completion endpoints, and streamed responses.
join.ef: Exposes agent execution through HTTP APIs, compatible completion endpoints, and streamed responses.
join.observation: The API adapter includes OpenAI-compatible chat-completions and Responses routes, run state, request identity, and result retrieval.

join.purpose: Participate as an agent in clients using the Agent Client Protocol.
join.function: Projects session creation, prompts, updates, permissions, history, and controls into ACP.
join.ef: Projects session creation, prompts, updates, permissions, history, and controls into ACP.
join.observation: The ACP gateway projection submits work to the profile gateway and translates its events; the connection acts as a viewer of daemon-owned execution.

join.purpose: Exchange task requests and responses as speech.
join.function: Transcribes speech input and synthesizes or streams spoken output through supported clients and providers.
join.ef: Transcribes speech input and synthesizes or streams spoken output through supported clients and providers.
join.observation: Voice memo transcription, local or cloud speech providers, streaming TTS, and voice-specific model routing are implemented. Meeting plugins add live meeting participation and transcript workflows.

join.purpose: Provide an animated companion within supported Hermes interfaces.
join.function: Maintains pet selection and animation state and supports creation of custom pet assets.
join.ef: Maintains pet selection and animation state and supports creation of custom pet assets.
join.observation: The pet engine serves CLI, TUI, and desktop surfaces; its generation pipeline constructs the animation atlas used by the companion.

join.purpose: Conduct agent conversations and deliver work through external communication channels.
join.function: Manages messaging adapters, routes inbound events to sessions, and delivers replies, streams, media, and notifications.
join.ef: Manages messaging adapters, routes inbound events to sessions, and delivers replies, streams, media, and notifications.
join.observation: GatewayRunner manages adapter lifecycles and profile routing. Channel policies, pairing, session keys, busy-input handling, streaming, and delivery are coordinated with canonical session execution.

join.purpose: Receive channel events and send results to their intended conversation destinations.
join.function: Provides platform messaging APIs, connection events, and supported media or interactive-message facilities.
join.ef: Provides platform messaging APIs, connection events, and supported media or interactive-message facilities.
join.observation: Bundled platform plugins include Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal, Teams, and additional channels; their adapters translate platform-specific behavior into the shared gateway contract.

join.purpose: Start or inform work from configured external events.
join.function: Receives webhook deliveries, applies subscription routing, and admits the resulting event into agent execution.
join.ef: Receives webhook deliveries, applies subscription routing, and admits the resulting event into agent execution.
join.observation: Webhook handling includes filters, coalescing, delivery behavior, and the receiving side of optional MCP event subscriptions.

join.purpose: Add or replace capabilities without incorporating every integration into the agent core.
join.function: Discovers and loads plugins that register tools, hooks, providers, commands, middleware, and interface contributions.
join.ef: Discovers and loads plugins that register tools, hooks, providers, commands, middleware, and interface contributions.
join.observation: Plugin sources include bundled packages, profile packages, opted-in project packages, and Python entry points. Memory and context-engine plugins have specialized discovery paths.

join.purpose: Make selected external accounts and installable capabilities available to a conversation.
join.function: Discovers connection targets, conducts connection operations, and installs selected catalog plugins or skills.
join.ef: Discovers connection targets, conducts connection operations, and installs selected catalog plugins or skills.
join.observation: Connection operations are backend-owned and tied to profile and session identity. Managed accounts and local MCP connections converge on the connector lifecycle and ordinary tool dispatch.

join.purpose: Install, configure, maintain, and diagnose the environment in which the agent runs.
join.function: Coordinates configuration, isolated profiles, managed dependencies, updates, and operational diagnostics.
join.ef: Coordinates configuration, isolated profiles, managed dependencies, updates, and operational diagnostics.
join.observation: Source installers, desktop packaging, container and Nix definitions, and runtime bootstrap paths provide different deployment implementations of the same operational purpose.

join.purpose: Apply selected behavior and account settings to the correct isolated profile.
join.function: Loads, validates, migrates, and writes configuration and manages profile-specific state locations.
join.ef: Loads, validates, migrates, and writes configuration and manages profile-specific state locations.
join.observation: Configuration separates ordinary settings from secret-bearing environment values. Profiles isolate state while supported gateway multiplexing serves several profiles in one process.

join.purpose: Supply a reproducible, compatible set of application and tool dependencies.
join.function: Resolves locked packages, acquires and verifies artifacts, builds environments, and publishes usable runtime generations.
join.ef: Resolves locked packages, acquires and verifies artifacts, builds environments, and publishes usable runtime generations.
join.observation: PM owns Python and tool environments, package storage, plugin dependency composition, compatibility handling, recovery, and platform-specific executable acquisition.

join.purpose: Move an installation to an available application version and restore the appropriate running services.
join.function: Checks update channels, prepares version changes, commits the update, and coordinates restart or recovery.
join.ef: Checks update channels, prepares version changes, commits the update, and coordinates restart or recovery.
join.observation: Update ownership depends on installation method; source updates and packaged desktop updates use their respective publication and replacement mechanisms.

join.purpose: Explain runtime health, execution failures, and resource or usage behavior.
join.function: Collects diagnostics, presents logs and usage, runs supported checks, and exports configured monitoring or metrics.
join.ef: Collects diagnostics, presents logs and usage, runs supported checks, and exports configured monitoring or metrics.
join.observation: Doctor, verification recipes, account-usage views, liveness tracking, local metrics, and configured telemetry serve diagnosis. Tests and evaluation probes provide supporting evidence rather than additional agent capabilities.

join.purpose: Produce reusable records of agent behavior over individual tasks or datasets.
join.function: Records agent trajectories and runs dataset prompts through parallel, resumable agent execution.
join.ef: Records agent trajectories and runs dataset prompts through parallel, resumable agent execution.
join.observation: Batch execution uses the same AIAgent implementation as interactive work. Toolset distributions and trajectory conversion shape the generated research records.

join.purpose: Fit recorded agent trajectories into a target training or processing budget.
join.function: Protects selected trajectory boundaries and summarizes the necessary middle material.
join.ef: Protects selected trajectory boundaries and summarizes the necessary middle material.
join.observation: Trajectory compression is an offline post-processing function distinct from reducing the active conversation context. It supports asynchronous processing and directory-level workloads.
